## Special-Purpose Datasets in SDTM

Special-Purpose datasets are a distinct category of SDTM datasets that exist alongside the three General Observation Classes (Interventions, Events, Findings). They have specific standardized structures to represent additional important information beyond what the general observation classes cover.

### Definition

According to the SDTM model:

> "In addition to the 3 general observation classes, a submission will generally include a set of other special-purpose datasets of specific standardized structures to represent additional important information. A Demographics special-purpose domain is included with human and animal studies. Other special-purpose domains may be included."

**[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md]**

### Domains in the Special-Purpose Category

Based on the SDTM Domain Abbreviation codelist (C66734) and the SDTMIG v3.4 structure, the following domains are classified as Special-Purpose:

| Domain Code | Domain Name | Description |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| **CO** | Comments | Contains comments that may be collected alongside other data |
| **DM** | Demographics | Includes essential standard variables that describe each subject; it is the parent domain for all other observations for human clinical subjects |
| **SE** | Subject Elements | One record per actual Element per subject |
| **SM** | Subject Disease Milestones | One record per Disease Milestone per subject |
| **SV** | Subject Visits | One record per actual or planned visit per subject |

**[Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md — C66734 SDTM Domain Abbreviation]**

Additionally, the following are also classified as Special-Purpose in the broader SDTM model:

| Domain Code | Domain Name | Description |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| **DI** | Device Identifiers | Contains information that identifies a specific device unit (classified as a study reference dataset since SDTM v1.7) |
| **DR** | Device-Subject Relationships | Contains the linkage of each subject to the device(s) to which they may have been exposed |

**[Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md — C66734]**

### Dataset Structure (from Dataset-level Metadata)

| Dataset | Structure | Keys |
|---------|-----------|------|
| CO | One record per comment per subject | STUDYID, USUBJID, IDVAR, COREF, COOTC |
| DM | One record per subject | STUDYID, USUBJID |
| SE | One record per actual Element per subject | STUDYID, USUBJID, ETCD, SESTDTC |
| SM | One record per Disease Milestone per subject | STUDYID, USUBJID, MIDS |
| SV | One record per actual or planned visit per subject | STUDYID, USUBJID, SVTERM |

**[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md — §3.2.1 Dataset-level Metadata]**

### Key Characteristics

1. **DM is the parent domain** — It is the foundational dataset for all other observations for human clinical subjects. **[Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md]**

2. **Special-Purpose vs. General Observation Classes** — SDTM datasets that represent data about study subjects are of 2 types: general observation class datasets and special-purpose datasets. **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]**

3. **Extensible set** — The special-purpose domains are marked as an extensible set, meaning additional special-purpose domains may be defined as needed. **[Source: model/01_concepts_and_terms.md — Concept Map]**

4. **DI reclassification** — The DI domain was originally classified as a special-purpose domain but since SDTM v1.7 has been reclassified as a study reference dataset. **[Source: domains/DI/assumptions.md]**

### Relationship to Other Dataset Types

The SDTM overall structure includes:
- **Subject Data**: General Observation Class domains (extensible) + Special-Purpose domains (extensible)
- **Associated Persons Data**
- **Study-Level Data**: Trial Design Model + Study Reference datasets
- **Relationship Datasets**: RELREC, SUPPQUAL, POOLDEF, RELSUB, etc.

**[Source: model/01_concepts_and_terms.md — Concept Map]**

The two-character domain code must follow these rules:

3. **No other characters** are allowed (e.g., no hyphens, underscores, or lowercase letters)

This restriction is for compatibility with SAS v5 transport files and with file naming requirements as part of the Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD).

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.2]**

## Prefix Usage

The 2-character domain identifier is used as a **prefix** in most variable names within that domain to minimize risk when merging/joining datasets. However, there are exceptions where variables are **not** prefixed with the domain identifier:

- Required Identifiers (STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID)
- Commonly used grouping and merge keys (e.g., VISIT, VISITNUM, VISITDY)
- All Demographics (DM) domain variables other than DMDTC and DMDY
- All variables in RELREC and SUPPQUAL, and some variables in the Comments and Trial Design datasets

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.2]**

## Custom Domain Codes

For sponsors creating custom domains, domain codes beginning with the letters **X, Y, or Z** have been reserved to avoid conflicts with future CDISC-defined codes. Any letter or number may be used in the second position. Note that using codes beginning with X, Y, or Z is optional, not required.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.6]**

## Standard Domain Codes

Standard domain codes are defined in the **SDTM Domain Abbreviation codelist (C66734)** in CDISC Controlled Terminology. Datasets are normally named to be consistent with the domain code (e.g., the Demographics dataset DM is named `dm.xpt`).

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.6]**

results.answer:
## Findings About Observation Class

The Findings About observation class is a **specialized subclass** of the standard Findings class, designed to capture **qualitative or quantitative findings about an event or intervention** that occurred at a prior time point. It is implemented through the **FA (Findings About Events or Interventions)** domain.

### Key Differences from Standard Findings Class

| Aspect | Standard Findings Class | Findings About (FA) Class |
|--------|------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Primary Purpose** | Direct measurements, observations, or assessments of a subject at a point in time | Findings that describe, characterize, or provide additional detail about a previously recorded **event** or **intervention** |
| **Subject of the Finding** | The subject (patient) | An event (e.g., AE, MH) or intervention (e.g., CM, EX) that happened to the subject |
| **Temporal Relationship** | The finding is about the subject's current state | The finding is **about** something that already occurred (retrospective or concurrent characterization) |
| **Key Identifier Variables** | `--TESTCD`, `--TEST`, `--ORRES`, `--STRESC` | `FATESTCD`, `FATEST`, `FAORRES`, `FASTRESC` **plus** `FAOBJ` (the object of the finding) |
| **Relationship to Other Domains** | Standalone domain | Requires linkage via `STUDYID`, `USUBJID`, and optionally `--REFID` or `RELREC` to the target event/intervention domain |

### FA Domain Variable Structure

The FA domain follows the standard Findings class template but adds the **`FAOBJ`** variable, which identifies the **object** of the finding (e.g., "ADVERSE EVENT", "CONCOMITANT MEDICATION"). **[Source: domains/FA/spec.md]**

Key variables include:
- **FAOBJ** — The object of the finding (e.g., "ADVERSE EVENT", "MEDICAL HISTORY") — this is the distinguishing variable
- **FATESTCD/FATEST** — The short name/long name of the finding about the object
- **FAORRES/FASTRESC** — Original and standardized results
- **FAOBJ** is typically populated with a value from a controlled terminology codelist (e.g., C66742 for "ADVERSE EVENT")

### When to Use FA vs. Standard Findings

**Use FA when:**
- You need to record characteristics of an **adverse event** (e.g., severity, causality, action taken) that are not captured in the AE domain itself
- You need to record details about a **medical history condition** beyond what MH provides
- You need to record information about a **prior or concomitant medication** (e.g., reason for use, efficacy)
- The finding is **about** a record in another domain, not directly about the subject

**Use Standard Findings when:**
- The measurement or observation is directly about the **subject** (e.g., lab test, vital sign, ECG)
- The finding is a direct assessment of the subject's current state

### Relationship Mechanism

FA records are linked to their target event/intervention records using:
1. **`FAOBJ`** — Identifies the type of object (e.g., "ADVERSE EVENT")
2. **`--REFID`** (e.g., `FAREFID`) — References the identifier of the target record (e.g., `AESPID` from AE domain)
3. **`RELREC`** — The Related Records dataset can formally establish the relationship

**[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md; chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4]**

### Example

If an adverse event of "Headache" (recorded in AE) has a severity assessment of "Mild" that is captured separately, the FA domain would contain:
- `FAOBJ` = "ADVERSE EVENT"
- `FATESTCD` = "SEV" (Severity)
- `FAORRES` = "MILD"
- `FAREFID` = [AESPID from the AE record]

This differs from a standard Findings domain (e.g., VS) where `VSTESTCD` = "SYSBP" directly measures the subject's systolic blood pressure.

results.answer:
## Collected vs. Derived Data in SDTM

### Definition of Collected vs. Derived

**Collected data** refers to values that originate directly from a source such as a CRF, vendor, or device, without any sponsor-performed transformation or calculation. **Derived data** refers to values that are created through a sponsor-defined algorithm, calculation, or transformation of other data.

### Key Rules

1. **Values calculated by a central lab according to its procedures** are considered **collected** rather than derived. For example, a lab-derived value reported by a central lab goes into `--ORRES` and the derived flag (`--DRVFL`) should be null. **[Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md item_6]**

2. **QRS instrument total/subtotal scores** follow specific rules:
   - Scores listed on the CRF = captured data
   - Scores documented in instrument manuals/reference papers = captured data
   - Scores included in eData by sponsors = captured data (CT is extensible)
   - Any imputations/calculations done to produce total scores via transforming numeric responses = **ADaM derivations**, not SDTM
   - If operationally derived by the sponsor, `--DRVFL` must be set to "Y"
   - If received from a central provider/vendor, the value goes into `--ORRES` and `--DRVFL` is null **[Source: domains/QS/assumptions.md item_4; domains/FT/assumptions.md item_4]**

3. **Values calculated and reported by a lab** according to its procedures are considered collected; the Derived Flag (`--DRVFL`) should be null for these results. **[Source: domains/CP/assumptions.md item_3]**

### Indicating Origin of Variable Values

The **origin** of a variable value is indicated using the **Define-XML file**, not within the SDTM dataset itself. The origin element in Define-XML communicates to the reviewer where the data originated. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.8.1]**

Allowable origin values include:
- **Collected** — from CRF, vendor, or device (should be traceable to an annotated CRF)
- **Derived** — from some derivation algorithm (should be traceable to the algorithm)
- **Assigned** — from study-level assignment

### Handling Mixed Origins

When both collected and derived values appear in the **same variable** (e.g., QS domain where some records are CRF-collected and others are derived total scores), the origin must be described using **value-level metadata** in the Define-XML document. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.8.2]**

### Summary Table

| Scenario | Considered | `--DRVFL` | Origin in Define-XML |
|----------|-----------|-----------|----------------------|
| Value entered on CRF by investigator | Collected | Null | Collected |
| Value calculated by central lab per their procedures | Collected | Null | Collected |
| Value received from central vendor | Collected | Null | Collected |
| Value derived by sponsor via algorithm | Derived | "Y" | Derived |
| Investigator-derived score written on CRF | Collected | Null | Collected |
| QRS total score from eData (not on CRF) | Captured | Null | Collected |

## Trial Design Model Datasets in SDTM

The Trial Design Model (TDM) is one of the two types of study-level data in SDTM (the other being Study Reference Data). It provides a standardized way to describe the planned conduct of a clinical trial, as shown in study design diagrams and schedule of assessments tables. **[Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]**

### Datasets

The Trial Design Model consists of the following 8 datasets:

| Dataset | Name | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| **TA** | Trial Arms | Defines the planned paths (arms) through the trial, divided into study cells (arm × epoch combinations) |
| **TE** | Trial Elements | Describes the distinct periods or elements within the trial (e.g., screening, treatment, follow-up) |
| **TV** | Trial Visits | Lists the planned visits and their timing relative to trial elements |
| **TD** | Trial Disease Assessments | Describes planned disease assessment schedules |
| **TM** | Trial Disease Milestones | Defines planned disease-related milestones (e.g., progression, response) |
| **TI** | Trial Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria | Contains all inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial |
| **TS** | Trial Summary | Provides summary characteristics of the trial (e.g., design type, blinding, control type) |
| **TT** | Trial Trial (not listed in the retrieved context but part of the model) | Describes planned treatment strategies |

**[Source: domains/TA/spec.md, domains/TD/spec.md, domains/TE/spec.md, domains/TI/spec.md, domains/TM/spec.md, domains/TS/spec.md, domains/TV/spec.md]**

### Purpose and Information Captured

The TDM captures the following kinds of study-level information **[Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md §7.1.1]**:

1. **Study Design Structure** — The overall plan and design of the study, including arms, epochs, and study cells (the combination of arm and epoch)
2. **Planned Subject Paths** — Each arm represents a planned path through the trial, covering the entire duration of subject participation
3. **Epoch Definitions** — The division of the trial into periods of time that serve specific purposes (e.g., screening, treatment, washout, follow-up)
4. **Visit Schedule** — Planned visits and their timing relative to trial elements
5. **Eligibility Criteria** — All inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial (TI), which may not be fully represented in subject-level IE data
6. **Trial Characteristics** — Summary-level information about the trial design (TS), such as design type, blinding, and control type
7. **Disease Assessment Plans** — Planned disease assessments and milestones (TD, TM)

### Key Benefits

The standardized TDM allows reviewers to **[Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md §7.1.1]**:
- Clearly and quickly grasp the design of a clinical trial
- Compare the designs of different trials
- Search a data warehouse for clinical trials with certain features
- Compare planned and actual treatments and visits for subjects in a clinical trial

### Relationship to Subject-Level Data

The TDM datasets are study-level (not subject-level) and describe the **planned** conduct of the trial. They are used in conjunction with subject-level data (e.g., SE for Subject Elements, SV for Subject Visits) to compare planned versus actual subject experiences. The TI dataset specifically provides information that may not be present in the subject-level IE (Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria Not Met) domain, which only records criteria that subjects did not meet. **[Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md]**

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, date and time variables in SDTM are formatted according to the **ISO 8601 extended format** and use the **DTC** suffix.

## Format

Date/time variables are stored as **character** (Char) data types and must use the **ISO 8601 extended format**, which requires hyphen delimiters for date components and colon delimiters for time components. The basic format (without delimiters) is **not** permitted. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.1]**

The ISO 8601 representation follows this pattern:

```
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss(.n+)?(((+|-)hh:mm)|Z)?
```

Where:
- `YYYY` = four-digit year
- `MM` = two-digit month (01-12)
- `DD` = two-digit day (01-31)
- `T` = time designator (indicates time information follows)
- `hh` = two-digit hour (00-23, am/pm NOT allowed)
- `mm` = two-digit minute (00-59)
- `ss` = two-digit second (00-59)
- `(.n+)?` = optional fractional seconds
- `(((+|-)hh:mm)|Z)?` = optional time zone

**Spaces are not allowed** in any ISO 8601 representations. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.1]**

## Suffix

The SDTM fragment employed for date/time character variables is **DTC**. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.1]**

This suffix is used in variable names such as:
- `--DTC` — Date/Time of Collection (primary date/time for the observation)
- `--STDTC` — Start Date/Time of Observation
- `--ENDTC` — End Date/Time of Observation

These are classified as **Timing** variables in the SDTM model. **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.5]**

## Precision

Precision is handled through the ISO 8601 standard by the presence or absence of components. Missing components are represented by right truncation or a hyphen (for intermediate missing components). If date and time are completely missing, the field should be null. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.2]**

Examples of precision levels:
- `2003-12-15T13:14:17.123` — Date/time with fractional seconds
- `2003-12-15T13:14:17` — Date/time to nearest second
- `2003-12-15` — Date only (unknown time)
- `2003-12` — Year and month only

results.answer:
## MedDRA Coding Chain for Adverse Events

The MedDRA coding chain for adverse events in SDTM progresses from the verbatim collected term through multiple levels of the MedDRA hierarchy, each represented by specific variables in the AE domain.

### 1. Verbatim Term (AETERM)

**AETERM** captures the exact verbatim term as collected on the CRF. It is the **Topic** variable for the AE domain, **Required** (Core: Req), and must always have a value. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AETERM]**

### 2. Modified Reported Term (AEMODIFY)

**AEMODIFY** is a **Permissible** (Core: Perm) **Synonym Qualifier** variable. It should be included if the sponsor's procedures permit modification of a verbatim term to aid in coding. The variable should be populated per sponsor procedures; null values are permitted. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2.b]**

### 3. Lowest Level Term (AELLT) and Code (AELLTCD)

- **AELLT** (Lowest Level Term): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier**, controlled by MedDRA. Represents the most granular level in the MedDRA hierarchy. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AELLT]**
- **AELLTCD** (Lowest Level Term Code): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier** of AELLT, controlled by MedDRA. The dictionary-derived numeric code for the LLT. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AELLTCD]**

### 4. Preferred Term (AEDECOD) and Code (AEPTCD)

- **AEDECOD** (Dictionary-Derived Term): **Required** (Core: Req), **Synonym Qualifier**. This is the dictionary-derived text description of AETERM or AEMODIFY, equivalent to the Preferred Term (PT) in MedDRA. The sponsor must provide the dictionary name and version in Define-XML. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEDECOD]**
- **AEPTCD** (Preferred Term Code): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier** of AEDECOD, controlled by MedDRA. The dictionary-derived code for the preferred term. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEPTCD]**

### 5. High Level Term (AEHLT) and Code (AEHLTCD)

- **AEHLT** (High Level Term): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier**, controlled by MedDRA. A grouping level above PT in the MedDRA hierarchy. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEHLT]**
- **AEHLTCD** (High Level Term Code): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier** of AEHLT, controlled by MedDRA. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEHLTCD]**

### 6. High Level Group Term (AEHLGT) and Code (AEHLGTCD)

- **AEHLGT** (High Level Group Term): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier**, controlled by MedDRA. A grouping level above HLT. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEHLGT]**
- **AEHLGTCD** (High Level Group Term Code): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier** of AEHLGT, controlled by MedDRA. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEHLGTCD]**

### 7. Body System or Organ Class (AEBODSYS) and Code (AEBDSYCD)

- **AEBODSYS** (Body System or Organ Class): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Record Qualifier**. Represents the SOC from the coding dictionary as assigned by the sponsor for analysis. This may differ from the primary SOC designated in MedDRA's standard hierarchy. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2.d]**
- **AEBDSYCD** (Body System or Organ Class Code): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier** of AEBODSYS, controlled by MedDRA. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEBDSYCD]**

### 8. Primary System Organ Class (AESOC) and Code (AESOCCD)

- **AESOC** (Primary System Organ Class): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier**. Represents the dictionary-derived primary SOC. In cases where the primary SOC was used for analysis, AEBODSYS and AESOC are the same. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — §4.3.5]**
- **AESOCCD** (Primary System Organ Class Code): **Expected** (Core: Exp), **Variable Qualifier** of AESOC, controlled by MedDRA. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AESOCCD]**

### Summary of the Coding Chain

```
AETERM (Verbatim)
    ↓
AEMODIFY (Modified, if applicable)
    ↓
AELLT / AELLTCD (Lowest Level Term)
    ↓
AEDECOD / AEPTCD (Preferred Term) ← Required
    ↓
AEHLT / AEHLTCD (High Level Term)
    ↓
AEHLGT / AEHLGTCD (High Level Group Term)
    ↓
AEBODSYS / AEBDSYCD (Body System/Organ Class — sponsor-assigned SOC)
AESOC / AESOCCD (Primary System Organ Class — dictionary-derived)
```

### Key Rules

1. **AEDECOD is Required** — must always be populated with the MedDRA Preferred Term. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEDECOD]**
2. **AEBODSYS is Expected** — represents the SOC used for the sponsor's analysis, which may differ from the primary SOC. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2.d]**
3. **AESOC is Expected** — represents the dictionary-derived primary SOC. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — §4.3.5]**
4. **Intermediate levels** (LLT, HLT, HLGT) and their codes are **Expected** — they should be represented when MedDRA is used. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — §4.3.5]**
5. **Dictionary metadata** — the sponsor must provide the dictionary name (e.g., MedDRA) and version in Define-XML using the external codelist element. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AEDECOD]**

### Example from Implementation

From the AE example data:
- AETERM = "POUNDING HEADACHE" → AEMODIFY = "Headache" → AEDECOD = "Headache" → AEBODSYS = "Nervous system disorders" **[Source: domains/AE/examples.md — Example 1]**

results.answer:
## Difference Between RFSTDTC/RFENDTC and RFXSTDTC/RFXENDTC

### RFSTDTC / RFENDTC (Subject Reference Start/End Date/Time)
- **Role:** Record Qualifier
- **Core:** Expected
- **Definition:** Sponsor-defined reference period. Usually represents the date/time of first and last study exposure, but **is open to customization** based on study design. **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10a]**
- **Customization examples:** In studies with a washout period before randomization, or where a medical procedure is required during screening (e.g., biopsy), RFSTDTC may be the enrollment date (prior to first dose). **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10a]**
- **Impact:** Study day values (--DY) are calculated using RFSTDTC, so if RFSTDTC is not the first dose date, study days will not be based on first dose. **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10a]**

### RFXSTDTC / RFXENDTC (Date/Time of First/Last Study Treatment)
- **Role:** Record Qualifier
- **Core:** Expected
- **Definition:** A **consistent, non-customizable** reference period for all interventional studies. RFXSTDTC and RFXENDTC **always** represent the date/time of first and last study exposure. **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10b]**
- **Key guarantee:** This pair ensures that a reviewer can **always** reference the first and last study exposure period, even if RFSTDTC has been customized to a different milestone. **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10b]**
- **Alignment:** RFXSTDTC should be the same as SESTDTC for the first treatment element in SE; RFXENDTC may equal SEENDTC for the last treatment element. **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10b]**
- **Source values:** RFXSTDTC equals the earliest EXSTDTC; RFXENDTC equals the latest EXENDTC (or EXSTDTC if EXENDTC is missing). **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFXSTDTC, RFXENDTC]**

### Summary of Key Difference

| Aspect | RFSTDTC/RFENDTC | RFXSTDTC/RFXENDTC |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Customization | Sponsor-defined, customizable | Fixed, always first/last exposure |
| Consistency | May vary by study design | Consistent across all interventional studies |
| Reviewer guarantee | Not guaranteed to be exposure-based | Guaranteed to be exposure-based |

---

## When RFSTDTC Will Be Null

RFSTDTC will be null for subjects who are **not treated** or **not exposed to study treatment**, specifically:

1. **Screen failures** — subjects with ARMNRS = "SCREEN FAILURE" **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9]**
2. **Enrolled but not assigned** — subjects with ARMNRS = "NOT ASSIGNED" **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9]**
3. **Randomized but not treated** — subjects with ARMNRS = "NOT TREATED" **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9]**

### Exception for Non-Interventional Studies
For studies with designs where a substantial portion of subjects are not expected to be treated (e.g., non-interventional/observational studies, studies with a no-treatment arm, or studies with a delay between randomization and treatment), a **different protocol milestone** may be chosen as RFSTDTC instead of first exposure. In such cases, RFSTDTC would not be null for untreated subjects because it is based on a different milestone. **[Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9]**

### Normal Range Representation (LBORNRLO and LBORNRHI)

- **LBORNRLO** (Reference Range Lower Limit in Orig Unit) and **LBORNRHI** (Reference Range Upper Limit in Orig Unit) are used to define the normal reference range for a continuous laboratory measurement in its original units. **[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBORNRLO] [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBORNRHI]**

- **LBNRIND** (Reference Range Indicator) is a variable that indicates where a specific result falls with respect to the defined reference range (e.g., from `LBORNRLO` and `LBORNRHI`). **[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBNRIND] [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_3]**

- **Type:** Char

- **Core:** Expected (Exp)

results.answer:
## QS Domain: QSCAT and QSTESTCD Roles

### QSCAT — Category of Question

**QSCAT** is a **Required** variable (Core: Req) that identifies the specific questionnaire instrument. Its definition:

- **Label:** Category of Question
- **Type:** Char
- **Controlled Terms:** C100129 (Category of Questionnaire)
- **Role:** Grouping Qualifier
- **Core:** Req

**[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — QSCAT]**

QSCAT serves as the primary grouping mechanism for questionnaire data. Examples include "ADAS-COG", "MDS-UPDRS", "BPI SHORT FORM", and "APACHE II" **[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — QSCAT; domains/QS/assumptions.md — item_1]**. The CDISC Controlled Terminology codelist for QSCAT values is "Category of Questionnaire" (C100129) **[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — Controlled Terminology]**.

### QSTESTCD — Question Short Name

**QSTESTCD** is the **Topic variable** for the QS domain, serving as the primary identifier for individual questions:

- **Label:** Question Short Name
- **Type:** Char
- **Controlled Terms:** Published separately per questionnaire
- **Role:** Topic
- **Core:** Req
- **Constraints:** Max 8 characters, cannot start with a number, only letters/numbers/underscores allowed

**[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — QSTESTCD]**

QSTESTCD values are published in separate codelists for each questionnaire instrument (e.g., "ADCCMD01", "BPR0103") **[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — QSTESTCD]**.

### How They Work Together

1. **Hierarchical Organization:**
   - **QSCAT** groups questions by instrument (e.g., "ADAS-COG")
   - **QSSCAT** (Permissible) provides subcategories within an instrument (e.g., "MENTAL HEALTH", "DEPRESSION", "WORD RECALL") **[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — QSSCAT]**
   - **QSTESTCD/QSTEST** identify individual questions within the instrument

2. **Instrument-Specific Variables via SUPPQUAL:**
   When QS needs to carry instrument-specific variables not in the standard QS structure, **SUPPQUAL** is used with **QSCAT as the linking variable (IDVAR)**. For example, questionnaire language (QSLANG) is stored in SUPPQS with `IDVAR = QSCAT` and `IDVARVAL = "BPI"` or `"ADAS-COG"` **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/examples.md — Example 2; chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.4.3 Examples]**.

3. **Domain Splitting by QSCAT:**
   QS data can be split into separate datasets by QSCAT value (e.g., QS36 for SF-36). When split:
   - DOMAIN remains "QS"
   - Dataset names become up to 4 characters (e.g., "QS36")
   - SUPP-- datasets are also split (e.g., "SUPPQS36")
   - --SEQ must remain unique across all split datasets within USUBJID

   **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.7 Splitting Domains]**

4. **Data Structure:**
   - **Vertical format:** One record per question per subject per time point
   - **QSTESTCD** enables conversion to horizontal format (as column names)
   - **QSTEST** provides the human-readable question name (max 40 chars)

   **[Source: domains/QS/spec.md — QSTESTCD, QSTEST]**

### Summary

| Variable | Role | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| QSCAT | Grouping Qualifier (Req) | Identifies the questionnaire instrument (CT: C100129) |
| QSSCAT | Grouping Qualifier (Perm) | Subcategory within instrument |
| QSTESTCD | Topic (Req) | Short code for individual question (max 8 chars) |
| QSTEST | Synonym Qualifier (Req) | Full question name (max 40 chars) |

QSCAT provides the instrument-level grouping that enables both SUPPQUAL linking and domain splitting, while QSTESTCD serves as the topic identifier for individual question-level data within the vertical QS structure.

The DS (Disposition) domain belongs to the **Events** general observation class. This is indicated in the variable index entry for DS, which labels it as "DS — Disposition (Events)" **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md]**.

The domain is structured as a flat file with rows representing observations and columns representing variables, consistent with the SDTM model **[Source: model/01_concepts_and_terms.md]**. The variables in the DS domain, as listed in the variable index, include:

### Role of DSTERM

The variable **DSTERM** has the role of **Topic** and a core of **Required (Req)** **[Source: domains/DS/spec.md]**.

## PR (Procedures) Domain — Purpose and PRTRT Variable

### Domain Purpose

The PR (Procedures) domain is used to represent **all collected procedures** performed on a subject during a study, regardless of the extent of physiological effect or whether the effect is observable or microscopic. It is based on the **Interventions observation class**.

Examples of procedures include:
- Disease screening (e.g., mammogram, pap smear)
- Endoscopic examinations (e.g., arthroscopy, colonoscopy, laparoscopy)
- Diagnostic tests (e.g., biopsy, catheterization, CT scan, MRI, pulmonary function test)
- Therapeutic procedures (e.g., ablation therapy, mechanical ventilation, radiation therapy)
- Surgical procedures (e.g., curative surgery, resection, stenting, implantation)

**[Source: domains/PR/assumptions.md — item_1]**

> **Important note:** Measurements obtained from procedures are represented in their respective **Findings** domains, not in PR. For example, a biopsy procedure is recorded in PR, while the histopathology findings from that biopsy are recorded in the Microscopic Findings (MI) domain. Relationships between PR and other domain records can be documented using RELREC.

**[Source: domains/PR/assumptions.md — item_1]**

---

### PRTRT — Reported Name of Procedure

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Reported Name of Procedure |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | **Req** (Required) |
| **Controlled Terms** | (None — free text) |
| **CDISC Notes** | Name of procedure performed, either preprinted or collected on a CRF. |

**[Source: domains/PR/spec.md — PRTRT]**

**Key points about PRTRT:**
- It is the **Topic variable** for the PR domain, meaning it identifies the fundamental concept being recorded (the procedure itself).
- It has a **Core of "Req"** (Required), meaning it must always be populated for every record in the PR domain.
- It accepts **free text** (verbatim values as collected on the CRF), with no controlled terminology codelist applied.
- The standardized/dictionary-derived version of the procedure name is stored in **PRDECOD** (Core: Perm), which references codelist C101858 (PROCEDUR).

**[Source: domains/PR/spec.md — PRTRT; domains/PR/spec.md — PRDECOD]**

## TS (Trial Summary) Domain Structure

The Trial Summary (TS) dataset allows the sponsor to submit a summary of the trial in a structured format. Each record contains the value of a parameter describing a characteristic of the trial — for example, trial phase, protocol title, and trial objectives. The TS dataset contains information about both planned and actual trial characteristics. **[Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md]**

### Variable Structure

The TS domain contains the following variables (in order):

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|
| TSSEQ | Sequence Number | Num | Identifier | Req |
| TSGRPID | Group ID | Char | Identifier | Perm |
| TSPARMCD | Trial Summary Parameter Short Name | Char | Topic | Req |
| TSPARM | Trial Summary Parameter | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req |
| TSVAL | Parameter Value | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp |
| TSVALNF | Parameter Value Null Flavor | Char | Result Qualifier | Perm |
| TSVALCD | Parameter Value Code | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp |
| TSVCDREF | Name of the Reference Terminology | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp |
| TSVCDVER | Version of the Reference Terminology | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp |

**[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — TS]**

### Key Structural Rules

- **Multiple records per parameter**: A trial may have multiple records for a single parameter (e.g., two records with TSPARMCD = "TTYPE" for safety and efficacy). Each record gets a unique TSSEQ value. **[Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md — item_12]**
- **TSVAL can be null** only when TSVALNF is populated. Text over 200 characters can be added to additional columns TSVAL1-TSVALn. **[Source: domains/TS/spec.md — TSVAL]**
- **TSVALCD** is populated only when there is controlled terminology for TSVAL (e.g., null for TSPARMCD = "PLANSUB" or "TITLE"). **[Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md — item_9]**
- **TSVAL values** may be numeric, datetimes, ISO8601 durations, or text. Some responses come from controlled terminology; others are free text. **[Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md — item_7]**

---

## TSPARMCD Variable

### Definition

- **Label:** Trial Summary Parameter Short Name
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Topic
- **Core:** Req (Required)
- **Controlled Terms Codelist:** C66738 (Trial Summary Parameter Test Code)
- **Length Limit:** 8 characters maximum

**[Source: domains/TS/spec.md — TSPARMCD]**

### CDISC Notes

TSPARMCD is the companion to TSPARM. It is limited to **8 characters** and does not have special character restrictions. These values should be short for ease of use in programming, but it is not expected that TSPARMCD will need to serve as variable names. Examples include "AGEMIN" and "AGEMAX". **[Source: domains/TS/spec.md — TSPARMCD]**

### Controlled Terminology

- **Codelist Code:** C66738 (Trial Summary Parameter Test Code)
- **Location:** The full list of values for TSPARMCD (and corresponding TSPARM values) is maintained in CDISC Controlled Terminology, available at https://www.cancer.gov/research/resources/terminology/cdisc. **[Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md — item_5]**
- **Extensibility:** Controlled terminology for TSPARM is **extensible** — sponsors may add parameters, but the meaning of any added parameters should be explained in the metadata for the TS dataset. **[Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md — item_6]**

### Companion Variable: TSPARM

- **Label:** Trial Summary Parameter
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Synonym Qualifier
- **Core:** Req
- **Controlled Terms:** C67152 (Trial Summary Parameter Test Name)
- **Length Limit:** 40 characters maximum
- **Examples:** "Planned Minimum Age of Subjects", "Planned Maximum Age of Subjects"

**[Source: domains/TS/spec.md — TSPARM]**

## CE (Clinical Events) Domain

### Observation Class

The CE (Clinical Events) domain belongs to the **Events** observation class. The Events class represents "planned protocol milestones such as randomization and study completion, and occurrences, conditions, or incidents independent of planned study evaluations occurring during the study (e.g., adverse events) or prior to the study (e.g., medical history)." **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md — 3.1.2 The Events Observation Class]**

The CE domain is based on the Events general observation class and "thus can use any variables in the Events class, including those found in the AE domain specification table." **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md — item_6]**

### Purpose

The CE domain captures clinical events that are not considered adverse events per protocol. These may include:
- Episodes of symptoms of the disease under study (e.g., migraine headaches in a migraine study)
- Events that do not constitute adverse events but might lead to identification of an AE
- Specific events tracked as efficacy endpoints (e.g., TIA, stroke, death in a stroke prevention study) **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md — item_1]**

### CETERM Variable Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Order** | 8 |
| **Label** | Reported Term for the Clinical Event |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Controlled Terms** | (none) |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Req |
| **CDISC Notes** | Term for the medical condition or event. Most likely preprinted on CRF. |

**[Source: domains/CE/spec.md — CETERM]**

CETERM is the **Topic variable** for the CE domain, meaning it identifies the event being reported. It is a **Required** variable (Core: Req) and represents the collected name for the clinical event observation. In the Events observation class model, the `--TERM` variable is defined as "The collected name for an event observation" with a Topic role. **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md — 3.1.2 The Events Observation Class]**

- **CEPRESP** — Clinical Event Pre-specified (Variable Qualifier, Perm, CT: C66742 — "Y" for prespecified)
- **CEOCCUR** — Clinical Event Occurrence (Record Qualifier, Perm, CT: C66742 — "Y"/"N" for solicited events)

results.answer:
Based on the provided context, the RELSUB (Related Subjects) dataset is used to represent relationships between two study subjects, and the RSUBJID variable holds the identifier of the related subject or pool.

### How RELSUB Represents Relationships Between Two Subjects

1.  **Scope**: RELSUB is specifically used to represent relationships between persons where **both are study subjects**. A relationship between a study subject and a non-subject cannot be represented here; that must be reported in APRELSUB. **[Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- item_1]**

2.  **Bidirectional Representation**: Every relationship between two study subjects is represented in RELSUB as **two directional records**:
    - Record 1: The first subject's identifier in `USUBJID` and the second subject's identifier in `RSUBJID`.
    - Record 2: The second subject's identifier in `USUBJID` and the first subject's identifier in `RSUBJID`.
    - The `SREL` values in the two records describe the same relationship but from the viewpoint of each subject (e.g., "MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL" and "CHILD, BIOLOGICAL"). **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions, item 7; domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- item_7]**

3.  **Multiple Relationships**: If two subjects have more than one relationship (e.g., a woman is both maternal aunt and wet nurse to an infant), each relationship is represented by its own pair of records in RELSUB. **[Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- item_8]**

4.  **Example**: In a hemophilia study with a mother (HEM021-001) and two children (HEM021-002, HEM021-003), the relationship is represented as follows:
    - Mother to Child 1: `USUBJID=HEM021-001`, `RSUBJID=HEM021-002`, `SREL=MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL`
    - Child 1 to Mother: `USUBJID=HEM021-002`, `RSUBJID=HEM021-001`, `SREL=CHILD, BIOLOGICAL`
    - Child 1 to Child 2: `USUBJID=HEM021-002`, `RSUBJID=HEM021-003`, `SREL=TWIN, DIZYGOTIC`
    - Child 2 to Child 1: `USUBJID=HEM021-003`, `RSUBJID=HEM021-002`, `SREL=TWIN, DIZYGOTIC` **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Example]**

### What the RSUBJID Variable Holds

- **Label**: Related Subject or Pool Identifier **[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- RSUBJID]**
- **Type**: Char **[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- RSUBJID]**
- **Role**: Identifier **[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- RSUBJID]**
- **Core**: Req (Required) **[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- RSUBJID]**
- **Value**: `RSUBJID` is populated with either the **USUBJID of the related subject** or the **POOLID of the related pool**. **[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- RSUBJID]**
- **Constraint**: The value in `RSUBJID` must be a `USUBJID` value present in the Demographics (DM) domain. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions, item 5]**

results.answer:
## PC and PP Domain Relationship

### Why Two Separate Domains

PC and PP are kept as separate domains because they represent **different topics** with **different data structures**, as described in the SDTMIG:

> "In the Pharmacokinetics domain example, the topic for PC is plasma (or other specimen) drug concentration as a function of time, and the structure is 1 record per analyte per time point per reference time point (e.g., dosing event) per subject. PP contains characteristics of the time-concentration curve (e.g., AUC, Cmax, Tmax, half-life) and elimination rate constant; the structure is 1 record per parameter per analyte per reference time point per subject."

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.6.2]**

This is explicitly cited as an example where a scientific area requires more than one data structure, similar to microbiology domains **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.6.2]**.

### Domain Characteristics

| Aspect | PC | PP |
|--------|----|----|
| **Class** | Findings | Findings |
| **Topic** | Specimen drug concentration as a function of time | Characteristics of the time-concentration curve |
| **Structure** | 1 record per analyte per time point per reference time point per subject | 1 record per parameter per analyte per reference time point per subject |
| **Nature** | Collected data (as collected) | Derived dataset (may be produced from analysis datasets) |

**[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- overview; domains/PP/assumptions.md -- item_1]**

### How They Relate

**1. Shared Dataset Relationship**

PC and PP are explicitly identified as "Shared Dataset" domains — PC provides the concentration data from which PP parameters are calculated:

- PC spec: "Shared Dataset: PP — pharmacokinetic concentrations → parameters" **[Source: domains/PC/spec.md -- Related Domains]**
- PP spec: "Shared Dataset: PC — pharmacokinetic parameters ← concentrations" **[Source: domains/PP/spec.md -- Related Domains]**

**2. RELREC Documentation Requirement**

Sponsors must document which PC records were used to calculate each PP parameter. This can be done via:

- Analysis dataset metadata, OR
- RELREC dataset documenting relationships between PC and PP records

**[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]**

**3. Four RELREC Methods**

The SDTMIG defines 4 methods for representing PC-PP relationships in RELREC:

| Method | Linking Variables | Relationship Type |
|--------|------------------|-------------------|
| **A** | PCGRPID and PPGRPID | Many-to-many |
| **B** | PCSEQ and PPGRPID | One-to-many |
| **C** | PCGRPID and PPSEQ | Many-to-one |
| **D** | PCSEQ and PPSEQ | One-to-one |

**[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]**

**4. Natural Key Considerations**

Both datasets share the same natural key components: **analyte** and **reference time point**. The `--GRPID` values must account for all combinations of analytes and reference time points, as both are part of the natural key for both datasets **[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]**.

**5. Decision Flow**

The SDTMIG provides a decision tree for determining the relationship approach:

> "Do all parameters for each PK profile use all concentrations for all subjects? If so, create a PPGRPID value for all PP records and a PCGRPID value for all PC records for each profile for each subject, analyte, and reference time point. Decide whether to relate datasets or records."

**[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_1]**

### Key Linking Variables

- **PCGRPID / PPGRPID**: Group IDs used to relate sets of records across domains
- **PCSEQ / PPSEQ**: Sequence numbers used for one-to-one or one-to-many relationships
- **PCRFTDTC / PPRFDTC**: Reference date/time that links PP records back to the PC reference time point **[Source: domains/PP/examples.md -- Example 1]**

### Summary

PC and PP are separate domains because they address **different scientific questions** (concentration vs. parameter) with **different record structures** (one per time point vs. one per parameter). The relationship between them is documented via RELREC using one of four methods, with the choice depending on whether all, some, or specific subsets of concentration data are used to calculate each parameter.

### What RDOMAIN identifies

**RDOMAIN** (Related Domain Abbreviation) identifies the **two-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s)**. In other words, it specifies which SDTM domain the associated parent record belongs to.

**Variable definition:**

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Related Domain Abbreviation |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Controlled Terms** | C66734 (SDTM Domain Abbreviation) |
| **Role** | Identifier (in RELREC, SUPPQUAL); Record Qualifier (in CO) |
| **Core** | Required (Req) in RELREC and SUPPQUAL; Permissible (Perm) in CO |

**[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md, domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md, domains/CO/spec.md]**

---

### Key differences by domain

| Domain | Role | Core | Notes |
|--------|------|------|-------|
| **RELREC** | Identifier | Req | Abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s) |
| **SUPPQUAL** | Identifier | Req | Two-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s) |
| **CO** | Record Qualifier | Perm | Two-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s). Null for comments collected on a general comments or additional information CRF page |

**[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md, domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md, domains/CO/spec.md]**

results.answer:
## Supplemental Qualifier Dataset Naming and Parent Domain Linkage

### Dataset Naming Convention

Supplemental Qualifier datasets are named using the pattern **SUPP--**, where "--" is replaced by the 2-character domain code of the parent domain. This creates a one-to-one correspondence between a domain dataset and its Supplemental Qualifier dataset **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2]**.

**Examples:**
- For Adverse Events (AE): `suppae.xpt`
- For Concomitant/Prior Medications (CM): `suppcm.xpt`

The single SUPPQUAL dataset option from SDTMIG v3.1 has been **deprecated** in favor of separate SUPP-- datasets per parent domain **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2]**.

### Variable That Ties Each SUPP-- Record Back to Its Parent Domain

The variable **RDOMAIN** (Related Domain Abbreviation) ties each SUPP-- record back to its parent domain.

**RDOMAIN Definition** (from [model/06_relationship_datasets.md]):

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Related Domain Abbreviation |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Identifier |
| **Core** | Required |
| **Controlled Terms** | (DOMAIN) — the 2-character domain abbreviation |

**CDISC Notes:** Two-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s) **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1]**.

### Complete Key Structure for Parent Record Linkage

A record in a SUPP-- dataset relates back to its parent record(s) via a composite key consisting of **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Key Rules]**:

1. **STUDYID** — Study Identifier
2. **RDOMAIN** — Related Domain Abbreviation (e.g., "AE", "CM")
3. **USUBJID** — Unique Subject Identifier
4. **IDVAR** — Identifying Variable (e.g., AESEQ, CMSEQ)
5. **IDVARVAL** — Identifying Variable Value

**Exception for Demographics (DM):** For SUPP-- records related to DM, both IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null because STUDYID, RDOMAIN, and USUBJID are sufficient to uniquely identify the parent record (DM has 1 record per USUBJID) **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**.

### Example

For `suppae.xpt`, RDOMAIN = "AE" identifies that the supplemental qualifiers belong to the Adverse Events domain. The IDVAR (e.g., AESEQ) and IDVARVAL specify which specific AE record within that domain the supplemental data applies to **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/examples.md -- Example 1]**.

## AP Domains: Linking Non-Subject Persons to Study Subjects

### Core Mechanism

AP (Associated Persons) domains link non-subject persons back to study subjects through **three dedicated linking variables**: `APID`, `RSUBJID`, and `SREL`. These variables are defined in the Associated Persons Data model and are used across all AP domains (e.g., APDM, APAE, APLB).

**[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — Overview]**

### Variable Definitions

#### APID (Associated Person Identifier)
- **Label:** Associated Persons Identifier
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req
- **CDISC Notes:** Identifier for a single associated person, a group of associated persons, or a pool of associated persons. If APID identifies a pool, POOLDEF records must exist for each associated person.

**[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — Variables Used in Associated Persons Data]**

#### RSUBJID (Related Subject or Pool Identifier)
- **Label:** Related Subject or Pool Identifier
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req
- **CDISC Notes:** Identifier used to identify a related subject or pool of subjects. RSUBJID will be populated with either the USUBJID of the related subject or the POOLID of the related pool.

**[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — Variables Used in Associated Persons Data]**
**[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md — RSUBJID]**

#### SREL (Subject, Device, or Study Relationship)
- **Label:** Subject, Device, or Study Relationship
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Record Qualifier
- **Core:** Req
- **Controlled Terms:** C100130 (RELSUB codelist)
- **CDISC Notes:** Describes the relationship of the subject identified in USUBJID or the pool identified in POOLID to the subject or pool identified in RSUBJID.

**[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md — SREL]**
**[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — Variables Used in Associated Persons Data]**

### How the Linking Works

The linking logic follows a **conditional pattern** based on which identifier is populated:

| Scenario | RSUBJID | RDEVID | SREL describes relationship to... |
|----------|---------|--------|-----------------------------------|
| Associated person related to a study subject | Populated with USUBJID | Null | The subject identified in RSUBJID |
| Associated person related to a device | Null | Populated with SPDEVID | The device identified in RDEVID |
| Associated person related to the study only | Null | Null | The study identified in STUDYID |

**[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — AP Domain Rules]**

### Key Rules

1. **APID replaces USUBJID**: In AP domains, `APID` is used as the identifier instead of `USUBJID` (which is used for study subjects). APID was removed from the general identifiers section because it is only allowed in AP domains.

   **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — AP Domain Rules]**

2. **RSUBJID must reference DM**: When populated, `RSUBJID` must be a `USUBJID` value present in the Demographics (DM) domain.

   **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — Assumptions, item 5]**

3. **SREL controlled terminology**: Values of `SREL` should be taken from the CDISC Controlled Terminology codelist `C100130` (RELSUB) wherever possible. If an appropriate term does not exist, another term may be used, but it should not be less specific than the verbatim term collected.

   **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — Assumptions, item 6]**

4. **Multiple relationships**: When an associated person has multiple collected relationships to a study subject or study subjects, those multiple relationships must be represented in the relationships dataset.

   **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md — Variables Used in Associated Persons Data]**

### Distinction from RELSUB

It is critical to note that **RELSUB** is used exclusively for relationships between **study subjects** (both persons are subjects). A relationship between a study subject and a person who is **not** a study subject may **not** be represented in RELSUB; this may only be reported in **APRELSUB** (the Associated Persons Related Subjects dataset).

**[Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md — item 1]**
**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — Assumptions, item 1]**

### APRELSUB Dataset Structure

The APRELSUB dataset formalizes these relationships with the following structure (one record per associated person relationship):

| Variable | Label | Type | Role |
|----------|-------|------|------|
| STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| APID | Associated Person Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| RSUBJID | Related Subject or Pool Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| RDEVID | Related Device Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| SREL | Subject, Device, or Study Relationship | Char | Record Qualifier |

**[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md — 6.6 Associated Persons Related Subjects (APRELSUB)]**

### Summary

- **RSUBJID** provides the **link** from the associated person (identified by `APID`) to a specific study subject (identified by `USUBJID` in DM).
- **SREL** provides the **semantic description** of that link (e.g., "MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL", "CAREGIVER", "DONOR").
- Together, they enable AP domains to represent data about non-subject individuals while maintaining traceability to the study subjects they are associated with.

results.answer:
## Convention for "Yes" and "No" Values in SDTM

### General Rule

Variables where the response is "Yes" or "No" ("Y" or "N") should **normally be populated for both "Y" and "N" responses**. This eliminates confusion regarding whether a blank response indicates "N" or is a missing value. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.3.7]**

### Exception: Single-Value Population

It is **permissible to populate only one value** ("Y" or "N") and leave the alternate value blank when the variable is collected or derived in a manner that allows only one response — such as when a single checkbox indicates "Yes" and the absence of a check is unambiguous.

**Example:** Last Observation Before Exposure Flag (--LOBXFL) — it is acceptable to use only a value of "Y" because "N" is not necessary to indicate that a value is not the last observation before exposure. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.3.7]**

### Extension to "U" and "NA"

Permissible values for variables with controlled terms of "Y" or "N" **may be extended** to include:
- **"U"** (Unknown)
- **"NA"** (Not Applicable)

...if it is the sponsor's practice to explicitly collect or derive values indicating "Unknown" or "Not Applicable" for that variable. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.3.7]**

### Controlled Terminology: No Yes Response (C66742)

The standard codelist for Yes/No responses is **C66742** (No Yes Response), which is **non-extensible** and contains four permitted values:

| Code | Submission Value | Meaning |
|------|-----------------|---------|
| C49487 | N | No |
| C48660 | NA | Not Applicable |
| C17998 | U | Unknown |
| C49488 | Y | Yes |

**[Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md — No Yes Response (C66742)]**

### Summary Table

| Scenario | Rule |
|----------|------|
| **Normal case** | Populate both "Y" and "N" responses |
| **Single-checkbox collection** (e.g., --LOBXFL) | May populate only "Y" |
| **Sponsor collects "Unknown" or "Not Applicable"** | May extend to include "U" or "NA" |
| **Controlled terminology** | Use C66742 (No Yes Response) — non-extensible, but "U" and "NA" are already included in the codelist |

Based on the retrieved context, the rules governing the two-character DOMAIN code in SDTM are as follows:

The two-character domain identifier (DOMAIN) is used as a prefix in most variable names to minimize risk when merging/joining domains for reporting purposes. When adding variables from the SDTM to standard domains or creating custom domains based on the general observation classes, sponsors must replace the "--" prefix in the SDTM tables of General Observation Class, Timing, and Identifier variables with the 2-character domain identifier value for that domain/dataset. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md]**

- **First character:** Limited to A-Z (letters only)

- Required Identifiers (STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID)
- Commonly used grouping and merge keys (e.g., VISIT, VISITNUM, VISITDY)
- All Demographics (DM) domain variables other than DMDTC and DMDY
- All variables in RELREC and SUPPQUAL, and some variables in the Comments and Trial Design datasets

Required identifiers are not prefixed because they are usually used as keys when merging/joining observations. The --SEQ and the optional Identifiers --GRPID and --REFID are prefixed because they may be used as keys when relating observations across domains. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md]**

| IDVAR | Identifying Variable | Char | Identifier | Req | Name of the identifying variable (e.g., --SEQ, --GRPID) |
| IDVARVAL | Identifying Variable Value | Char | Identifier | Exp | Value of identifying variable described in IDVAR |
| RELTYPE | Relationship Type | Char | Record Qualifier | Exp | Values: "ONE" or "MANY" (controlled terminology C78737) |
| RELID | Relationship Identifier | Char | Record Qualifier | Req | Unique value within USUBJID that identifies the relationship |

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1; domains/RELREC/spec.md]**

### How RELREC Works

A relationship is defined by:
1. Adding a record to RELREC for **each record to be related**
2. Assigning a **unique character identifier** (RELID) for the relationship
3. All records with the same RELID value within the same USUBJID are considered related

**[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**

### Two Types of Relationships

#### 1. Relating Peer Records (Subject-Level)
Records are specified using STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL. Examples of variables used in IDVAR:
- **--SEQ**: Unique record identifier within a domain
- **--GRPID**: Groups related records within a domain
- **--REFID**: Sponsor-defined or external identifier

**[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- Relating Peer Records]**

#### 2. Relating Datasets (Dataset-Level)
Used when information is split between datasets that need to be examined together. RELTYPE identifies the relationship type:
- **ONE**: Single record
- **MANY**: Multiple records

Possible combinations: ONE-to-ONE, ONE-to-MANY, MANY-to-ONE, MANY-to-MANY

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.3; model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1]**

### RDOMAIN Variable

**RDOMAIN** (Related Domain Abbreviation) is a **Required Identifier** variable that contains the 2-character domain abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s) in the relationship. For example:
- "AE" for Adverse Events
- "CM" for Concomitant Medications
- "LB" for Laboratory Test Results

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1; model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1]**

### Controlled Terminology

- **RDOMAIN**: Uses the SDTM Domain Abbreviation codelist (C66734) **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]**
- **RELTYPE**: Uses the Relationship Type codelist (C78737) **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]**

### Usage Examples

**Example 1:** Relating an AE record (AESEQ=5) to 2 CM records (CMSEQ=11, 12) using RELID=1:

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELID |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|-------|
| EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | 1 |
| EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 11 | 1 |
| EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 12 | 1 |

**[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md -- Example 1]**

### Special Use Cases

- **TR domain**: TRLNKGRP and TRLNKID are used with RELREC to link tumor/lesion results to response assessments (RS) and tumor identification (TU) records **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- items 1, 2]**
- **RS domain**: RSLNKGRP links findings domain records (e.g., TR, LB) that contribute to a response assessment record **[Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item 4]**
- **SS domain**: RELREC may link subject status assessments with data in other domains **[Source: domains/SS/assumptions.md -- item 2]**

### Important Notes

- RELREC is **not needed** for SUPP-- or CO datasets, as these already include parent record key identifiers **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.3]**
- RELREC should only represent **collected relationships** (explicit references, CRF checkboxes, or CRF design) **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**
- RELID values are sponsor-chosen but must be unique within USUBJID; a standard naming convention is recommended **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**

results.answer:
## Associated Persons in SDTM

### Definition

Associated Persons are individuals other than study subjects who can be associated with a study, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study. The structures of SDTM datasets that represent data about associated persons are based on the same structures used for study subject data — either general observation class structures (Interventions, Events, Findings) or special-purpose domain structures. **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

### AP Domain Naming Convention

AP domains use the domain code prefix `AP` followed by the relevant domain code. For example, associated persons demographics would use `APDM`. **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

This naming convention follows the standard SDTM domain naming rules where:
- Domain codes normally consist of 2 characters (e.g., DM, AE, LB)
- The 2-character domain identifier is used as a prefix in most variable names **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.2]**
- For AP domains, the prefix becomes `AP` + the standard domain code (e.g., APDM, APAE, APLB)

### Key Principles

1. **AP domains conform to the same general observation class models** (Interventions, Events, Findings) used for subject data
2. **The same variables, roles, and controlled terminology apply** as in standard SDTM domains
3. **AP-specific identifiers** are used instead of USUBJID:
   - **APID** — Associated Persons Identifier (replaces USUBJID)
   - **RSUBJID** — Related Subject or Pool Identifier (links to a subject or pool)
   - **RDEVID** — Related Device Identifier (links to a device via SPDEVID)
   - **SREL** — Subject, Device, or Study Relationship (describes the relationship type)
4. **AP domains are not part of the core SDTMIG for human clinical trials** — additional guidance is provided in the SDTM Implementation Guide: Associated Persons (SDTMIG-AP) **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

### Relationship to Standard Domain Codes

The standard SDTM domain codes (e.g., DM, AE, LB, CM) are defined in the SDTM Domain Abbreviation codelist (C66734). **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md; domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md; domains/CO/spec.md]** AP domains extend these by prepending "AP", creating domain codes like:
- APDM (Associated Persons Demographics)
- APAE (Associated Persons Adverse Events)
- APLB (Associated Persons Laboratory Test Results)
- APCM (Associated Persons Concomitant Medications)

The APRELSUB (Associated Persons Related Subjects) dataset is used to represent relationships between associated persons and study subjects. **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md §6.6]**

results.answer:
## Expected (Exp) Core Variable in SDTM

An **Expected (Exp)** variable is defined as "any variable necessary to make a record useful in the context of a specific domain." **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Core Rules for Expected Variables

| Attribute | Rule |
|-----------|------|
| **Inclusion in dataset** | Must always be included in the dataset |
| **Null values** | Allowed when data not collected or not applicable for a particular record |
| **Empty column** | If the study does not include the data item at all, a null column must still be included in the dataset |

### Define-XML Requirements When Data Item Is Not Collected

When a study does **not** collect the data item for an Expected variable, two actions are required:

1. **Include the column** in the dataset (with all null values)
2. **Add a comment** in the Define-XML document stating that the study does not include the data item

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Comparison with Other Core Designations

| Core | Must Include in Dataset? | Null Values Allowed? | Define-XML Comment Needed if Not Collected? |
|------|--------------------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| **Req** (Required) | Yes | No (cannot be null for any record) | N/A (must always be populated) |
| **Exp** (Expected) | Yes | Yes (when not available) | Yes — must state the study does not include the data item |
| **Perm** (Permissible) | Only if data collected | Yes | If not collected, do not include the variable or declare it in Define-XML |

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Key Distinction

The critical difference between Expected and Permissible variables regarding Define-XML handling:

- **Expected**: The column **must** appear in the dataset and be declared in Define-XML even if the study never collected the data. A comment explaining the absence of data is required.
- **Permissible**: If the study did not collect the data, the variable **should not** be included in the dataset and **should not** be declared in Define-XML at all. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

results.answer:
## Decision Criteria: Supplemental Qualifiers vs. Findings About (FA) Domain

The decision between storing assessments of an event as Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--) versus in the Findings About (FA) domain depends on **three key criteria** defined in the SDTMIG:

### Criterion 1: Timing Alignment with the Event

**If the assessment has the same timing as the event as a whole** → Use **Supplemental Qualifiers** (SUPP--)

**If the assessment has different timing from the associated event** → Use **FA domain**

Per Section 6.4.1: "A finding that is about part of an event, rather than the event as a whole, meets this criterion for the use of FA." Repeated assessments of disease or treatment-related symptoms, particularly intermittent symptoms, meet this criterion. **[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6]**

### Criterion 2: Number of Variables Required

**If the assessment requires only 1 variable for representation** → Use **Supplemental Qualifiers** (SUPP--)

**If the assessment requires more than 1 variable for its representation** → Use **FA domain**

The need to represent data requiring more than 1 variable in a findings about structure, rather than by adding 2 or more supplemental qualifiers to the parent record, is the basis for this criterion. **[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6]**

### Criterion 3: Pre-specified AEs

**If data indicate the occurrence of pre-specified AEs** → Use **FA domain**

Previous versions of the SDTMIG included the criterion "Data or information about an Event or Intervention that indicates the occurrence of a pre-specified AE." This has been replaced with Criterion 3 above. **[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6]**

---

## Additional Decision Framework

The following questions from Section 8.6.3 help determine placement **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3]**:

| Question | FA Domain | Supplemental Qualifiers |
|----------|-----------|------------------------|
| Is this a measurement with units? | Yes → FA | No → SUPP-- |
| What dates are collected? | Dates of assessments → FA | Start/end dates of event → SUPP-- |
| Does it apply to the event as a whole? | No (applies to part) → FA | Yes → SUPP-- |

---

## Built-in Qualifiers vs. FA

Some assessments of events (e.g., severity, relationship to study treatment) have been built into the SDTM Events model as qualifiers (e.g., --SEV, --TOXGR, --REASND). These are **not** treated as findings about events. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3]**

When FA is used to represent findings about a **part** of the event (different timing), the FATEST and FATESTCD values should be the same as the variable name and variable label in the corresponding event domain. For example, FATESTCD = "SEV" and FATEST = "Severity/Intensity". **[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_4]**

---

## Summary Decision Flow

1. **Does the assessment apply to the event as a whole?**
   - Yes → Consider SUPP-- (if 1 variable) or standard domain qualifier
   - No (different timing, part of event) → FA domain

2. **Does the assessment require >1 variable?**
   - No → SUPP-- possible
   - Yes → FA domain

3. **Is it a pre-specified AE occurrence?**
   - Yes → FA domain

4. **Is it a measurement with units at specific time points?**
   - Yes → FA domain

### --TESTCD (Findings domains)
- **Maximum length:** 8 characters

- **Maximum length:** 8 characters
- **Character restrictions:** **No special character restrictions** (unlike --TESTCD)
- **Purpose:** Short for ease of use in programming, but **not expected** to serve as a variable name
- **Source:** [domains/TS/spec.md]

### ARMCD (Trial Arms, Demographics, Trial Visits)
- **Maximum length:** **20 characters** (significantly longer)
- **Character restrictions:** **No special character restrictions** (unlike --TESTCD)
- **Purpose:** Accommodates complex values needed for crossover trials (e.g., 7-period crossover using 2-character treatment abbreviations with hyphens)

|----------|-----------|----------------------|---------------------------|

| ETCD | 8 | No | No |
| TSPARMCD | 8 | No | No |
| ARMCD | 20 | No | No |

results.answer:
## Relative Timing Variables in SDTM

The Relative Timing variables in SDTM are used to describe the timing of an observation relative to either a **sponsor-defined reference period** or a **specific reference time point**. They are defined in the Timing Variables for All Classes section of the SDTM model.

### Variables and Their Values

#### 1. Reference Period Variables (--STRF and --ENRF)

These describe timing relative to the **sponsor-defined study reference period**, which is the continuous period defined by RFSTDTC (start) and RFENDTC (end) in the Demographics (DM) dataset. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**

| Variable | Label | Allowable Values | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-----------------|---------|
| **--STRF** | Start Relative to Reference Period | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Start relative to the sponsor-defined reference period |
| **--ENRF** | End Relative to Reference Period | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | End relative to the sponsor-defined reference period |

**Controlled Terms Codelist:** C66728 (STENRF) **[Source: domains/CM/spec.md -- CMSTRF]**

**Important restrictions:**
- "COINCIDENT" and "ONGOING" are in the STENRF codelist but describe timing relative to a **point in time**, not an interval, so they are **not appropriate** for --ENRF. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**
- These variables should be used when information such as "PRIOR", "ONGOING", or "CONTINUING" is collected in lieu of a date. **[Source: domains/AG/spec.md -- AGSTRF]**

**Example:** A CRF checkbox indicating concomitant medication use began prior to the study reference period → CMSTRF = "BEFORE". **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**

#### 2. Reference Time Point Variables (--STRTPT, --STTPT, --ENRTPT, --ENTPT)

These describe timing relative to a **specific reference time point** (not the study reference period). They are useful when relative timing assessments are made at times other than the start/end of the study reference period. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**

| Variable | Label | Allowable Values | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-----------------|---------|
| **--STRTPT** | Start Relative to Reference Time Point | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Start relative to a specific reference time point |
| **--STTPT** | Reference Time Point | (free text) | Description of the reference time point for --STRTPT |
| **--ENRTPT** | End Relative to Reference Time Point | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, ONGOING, UNKNOWN | End relative to a specific reference time point |
| **--ENTPT** | Reference Time Point | (free text) | Description of the reference time point for --ENRTPT |

**Controlled Terms Codelist:** C66728 (STENRF) for --STRTPT and --ENRTPT **[Source: domains/RS/spec.md -- RSSTRTPT]**

**Important restrictions:**
- "DURING" and "DURING/AFTER" describe timing relative to an **interval**, not a point, so they are **not allowable** for --STRTPT/--ENRTPT. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**
- If the reference time point is the date of collection, **AFTER is not valid** for --STRTPT (would represent an event after collection). **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**

### Domain-Specific Usage Examples

| Domain | Typical Use | Source |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| **Medical History (MH)** | MHENRF for "Ongoing" relative to RFSTDTC; MHENRTPT/MHENTPT for "Ongoing" relative to screening visit date | **[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_5]** |
| **Adverse Events (AE)** | AEENRF for "Ongoing" relative to RFENDTC; AEENRTPT/AEENTPT for "Ongoing" relative to final safety follow-up | **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_5]** |
| **Clinical Events (CE)** | CESTRF/CEENRF for "Prior"/"Ongoing" relative to study reference period; CESTRTPT/CESTTPT/CEENRTPT/CEENTPT for other dates | **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_5]** |
| **Concomitant Medications (CM)** | CMSTRTPT/CMSTTPT/CMENRTPT/CMENTPT for medication use relative to specified time points (e.g., CMENRTPT = "ONGOING", CMENTPT = "2007-04-30") | **[Source: domains/CM/assumptions.md -- item_4]** |

### Summary of Value Restrictions

| Variable Group | Allowed Values | Not Allowed |
|----------------|----------------|-------------|
| --STRF, --ENRF | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | COINCIDENT, ONGOING |
| --STRTPT | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, UNKNOWN | DURING, DURING/AFTER |
| --ENRTPT | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, ONGOING, UNKNOWN | DURING, DURING/AFTER |

### Additional Relative Timing Variables

The model also includes:
- **--EVLINT**: Evaluation Interval (ISO 8601 duration or interval)
- **--EVINTX**: Evaluation Interval Text (text description when ISO 8601 cannot represent the interval) **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.5]**

### Caution on Derived Values

Sponsors are cautioned against deriving --STRF and --ENRF from collected dates for analysis purposes, as this may blur the distinction between collected and derived values. Analysis datasets are recommended for such derivations. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7]**

## DSDECOD Codelist for Disposition Events

For disposition events (when `DSCAT = "DISPOSITION EVENT"`), **DSDECOD** uses the **NCOMPLT** codelist (C66727), which is the "Completion/Reason for Non-Completion" codelist. **[Source: domains/DS/spec.md — DSDECOD]** **[Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md — item_3b]**

### Key Rules
- When `DSTERM = "COMPLETED"`, `DSDECOD` = `"COMPLETED"` from the NCOMPLT codelist. **[Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md — item_3b.i]**
- When `DSTERM` contains verbatim text (e.g., "Subject moved"), `DSDECOD` uses the **extensible** NCOMPLT codelist to map to a standardized term (e.g., `"LOST TO FOLLOW-UP"`). **[Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md — item_3b.ii]**

### Reason-for-Non-Completion Values

The NCOMPLT codelist (C66727) includes standardized terms such as:

| CDISC Submission Value | Description |
|------------------------|-------------|
| **ADVERSE EVENT** | Subject discontinued due to an adverse event |
| **DEATH** | Subject died |
| **LOST TO FOLLOW-UP** | Subject could not be contacted |
| **PHYSICIAN DECISION** | Physician decided to withdraw the subject |
